ABOUT THIS ATLAS

A country measured in people.

The population figures come from your supplied KOSIS workbook, table DT_1B040A3: Ministry of the Interior and Safety, Resident Registration Population, 1992–2025. Counts are at year-end and exclude foreigners. All regional totals reconcile with the national total.

How the shape is made

A numerical diffusion model expands high-density regions and contracts low-density regions. One shared deformation moves the coastline, borders, geographic grid and city locations. Density is assumed uniform within each reporting region. The finite raster and smoothing make displayed areas approximate; the numbers in the panel are the exact workbook values.

This is a regional cartogram, not a high-resolution population grid. The green lines are a regular geographic grid transformed by the population model; each cell does not represent an equal number of people. The geographic view restores the original map.

Historical boundaries

Geometry uses fixed 2013 KOSTAT boundaries from southkorea-maps. Counts retain the reporting boundaries of each year. Before 1997, Ulsan’s area shares South Gyeongsang’s density; before 2012, Sejong’s area shares South Chungcheong’s density. These are approximate spatial allocations, not reconstructed historical boundaries. Boundary transfers can affect comparisons.

The source also notes a population definition change in January 2010: registered persons with unknown residence are included from then onward.

Implementation: D3 / SVG rendering and precomputed diffusion meshes. Your original workbook has not been modified.
